newsitem.title: USA: Cocaine traces found in one of 200 Georgia babies.
newsitem.headline: Cocaine traces found in one of 200 Georgia babies.

text.p: One out of every 200 mothers who had given birth in Georgia had used cocaine shortly before their delivery, federal health officials said Thursday.

The U.S. Centres for Disease Control (CDC) said tests of dried blood spots from 14,968 newborn infants during a two-month period in 1994 found that 73, or almost 0.5 percent, had been exposed to cocaine in the womb.
The study was the first of its kind to study blood samples of newborn infants. Studies in other states have analysed urine specimens from women giving birth.
The CDC said maternal cocaine use during pregnancy can retard growth and cause early delivery, congenital anomalies and cerebral injury.
